title: Any action fails attempting to write to /var/lib/containers/
body:
### Issue Description

Attempting to run any command fails, since podman tries to write to `/var/lib/containers`, which is root-owned. Regular users cannot write into this path.

### Steps to reproduce the issue

```
> podman info --debug
Error: creating runtime static files directory "/var/lib/containers/storage/libpod": mkdir /var/lib/containers/storage: permission denied
```

### Describe the results you received

It fails writing into a system directory.

### Describe the results you expected

It should use the regular system directory.

### podman info output

```yaml
> podman info
Error: creating runtime static files directory "/var/lib/containers/storage/libpod": mkdir /var/lib/containers/storage: permission denied
```

### Podman in a container

No

### Privileged Or Rootless

Rootless

### Upstream Latest Release

Yes

### Additional environment details

This seems to be after an upgrade of podman (5.8.6-r0 -> 6.1.0-r0)

### Additional information

Additional information like issue happens only occasionally or issue happens with a particular architecture or on a particular setting

comments.body:
`/etc/containers/storage.conf` has:

    runroot = "/run/containers/storage"

Won't this break unless podman is running as root?

AFAIK, this is the default config shipped by containers-common.
Actually, deleting `/etc/containers/storage.conf` makes no difference, so perhaps this value is the build-in default too?
Previously reported at https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/29630, which op accidentally closed and cannot re-open.

https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/releases/tag/v6.0.0
https://blog.podman.io/2026/06/podman-6-configuration-file-changes/

There are very strict version requirements which must be follow strictly for proper functioning. You did not mention the distro but I guess alpine? You need to report these as packing issues. I guess it would also be nice if they could run basic automated testing before pushing out their package updates if that is a thing on alpine.


> Actually, deleting /etc/containers/storage.conf makes no difference, so perhaps this value is the build-in default too?

Deleting the file should work, the db however has logic to cache the storage paths so I wonder if the cache got poisoned by the incorrect config on first use. Not sure on the exact ordering in podman, if that is the case that is something we should avoid and only cache on success storage init.
So if this is a fresh install where you do not have any containers you may need to manually remove `~/.local/share/containers/storage/db.sql` and then run without this incorrect config file
